subDimensionName: Mission, theory of change and target segment
text: We can state in one sentence which entrepreneurs we serve, what problem we help them solve and what should change for them.
anchor0: No agreed statement; leaders give different answers when asked separately
anchor1: Target is described broadly (for example 'all SMEs') with no problem or change named
anchor2: A statement exists but misses one of: who, which problem, what changes
anchor3: Written statement covers who, problem and change, and two leaders give consistent answers
anchor4: Board approved statement names stage, sector and area and is reflected in selection criteria and reports
evidenceRequirement: Written mission or programme statement, plus separate interviews with two leaders compared with the selection criteria.
evidenceExamples: Mission statement or strategy page | Selection criteria sheet | Two leader interviews

subDimensionName: Mission, theory of change and target segment
text: We have a written theory of change that links our activities to the results we expect for entrepreneurs.
anchor0: No written theory of change or results framework
anchor1: Activities are listed in proposals but no link to expected results is shown
anchor2: A theory of change exists but its links have no stated assumptions
anchor3: Written theory of change shows activities, outputs, outcomes and key assumptions
anchor4: Written theory of change shows activities, outputs, outcomes and key assumptions, has an indicator for each outcome and keeps a dated version history
evidenceRequirement: The current theory of change or results framework and its version history.
evidenceExamples: Theory of change diagram or narrative | Logframe or results framework | Dated earlier versions

subDimensionName: Mission, theory of change and target segment
text: We have tested at least one assumption in our theory of change against our own data and changed the programme as a result.
anchor0: The theory of change has not been reviewed since it was written
anchor1: Reviewed informally in staff meetings with no record of changes
anchor2: Reviewed once, findings noted but no programme change followed
anchor3: Reviewed at least yearly using our own data, with at least one programme change recorded
anchor4: Reviewed at least yearly using our own outcome data and entrepreneur views, with a programme change recorded and re-checked the following year
evidenceRequirement: Review notes on the theory of change linked to a documented programme change.
evidenceExamples: Review meeting minutes | Programme change log | Revised curriculum or selection rule

subDimensionName: Mission, theory of change and target segment
text: Most enterprises we supported in the last twelve months fit the target segment in our written mission or strategy.
anchor0: Under 40 percent fit, or no written segment to check against
anchor1: 40 to 59 percent fit
anchor2: 60 to 74 percent fit
anchor3: 75 to 89 percent fit
anchor4: 90 percent or more fit, checked against the client database
evidenceRequirement: Written target segment definition and a client database extract with stage, sector and location. The verifier counts the share that fits.
evidenceExamples: Client database extract for last 12 months | Strategy page defining the segment
riskTag: Mission drift away from target segment

text: Our curriculum and support are adapted to the sectors, languages and business conditions of the enterprises we serve, not imported unchanged.
anchor0: Materials are imported from other programmes with no local change
anchor1: Some local examples added with no input from local entrepreneurs or practitioners
anchor2: Some modules adapted using staff knowledge only
anchor3: Curriculum adapted with documented input from local entrepreneurs, mentors or sector practitioners
anchor4: Curriculum adapted with documented local input, with local cases, language and sector data in the modules and a revision after each cohort
evidenceRequirement: Curriculum files compared with the original source materials, and records of local input.
evidenceExamples: Modules with local case studies | Notes of consultation with entrepreneurs or sector experts | Translated or local language materials

text: We chose our programme length, cohort size and support intensity deliberately for the enterprises we serve, and can explain why.
anchor0: Format copied from a funder or another programme with no rationale
anchor1: Format set by budget or convenience; rationale given only verbally
anchor2: A written rationale exists but is not linked to enterprise needs or evidence
anchor3: Written rationale links length, cohort size and intensity to enterprise needs and stage
anchor4: Written rationale links length, cohort size and intensity to enterprise needs and stage, draws on our own results or outside evidence, and the format was adjusted after a review
evidenceRequirement: Programme design note explaining length, cohort size and intensity, and any later adjustment.
evidenceExamples: Programme design paper | Cohort size decision note | Minutes of a design review

text: Our programme design includes scheduled peer learning among entrepreneurs in the same cohort.
anchor0: No peer learning; entrepreneurs meet only staff or mentors one to one
anchor1: Entrepreneurs meet at events but no peer sessions are planned
anchor2: Peer sessions are held occasionally, without structure or records
anchor3: Peer sessions are scheduled in every cohort with a facilitation guide and attendance records
anchor4: Peer sessions run in every cohort with a facilitation guide and attendance records, and entrepreneur feedback on them is collected and used to adjust later sessions
evidenceRequirement: Programme schedule showing peer sessions, with attendance records and feedback.
evidenceExamples: Cohort calendar | Peer session attendance sheets | Session feedback forms

text: We design new programmes around what target entrepreneurs tell us they need, not only around what funders offer to pay for.
anchor0: Programmes are designed only to match funder calls
anchor1: Entrepreneurs are consulted informally after the design is fixed
anchor2: Needs were gathered for some programmes but not written up
anchor3: A written needs assessment from target entrepreneurs informed each programme designed in the last two years
anchor4: A written needs assessment from target entrepreneurs informed each programme designed in the last two years, and a funded activity was reshaped or declined because it did not fit their needs
evidenceRequirement: Needs assessments or survey results dated before programme design, and an example of a design change driven by them.
evidenceExamples: Needs assessment report | Survey or focus group notes | Design change record

text: We know which other organisations serve the same enterprises in our area and how our offer differs from theirs.
anchor0: We do not know what other providers do
anchor1: Leaders can name a few providers but have not compared offers
anchor2: A list of providers exists but is out of date or lacks offer details
anchor3: Current list of providers with services and target groups, reviewed in the last 12 months
anchor4: Current list of providers with services and target groups, reviewed in the last 12 months, and our positioning and referral choices use the gaps and overlaps it shows
evidenceRequirement: Provider mapping or ecosystem map with a review date, and examples of referrals or positioning decisions based on it.
evidenceExamples: Ecosystem map | Provider comparison table | Referral log

text: We have an estimate of how many enterprises fit our target segment in our area and the share of them we reach each year.
anchor0: No estimate of the target population
anchor1: Rough figure quoted from memory with no source
anchor2: Estimate taken from a published or partner source but no reach share worked out
anchor3: Estimate with a named source and reach share calculated in the last 12 months
anchor4: Estimate with a named source and reach share calculated in the last 12 months, with reach share tracked yearly by area or sector and used to set targets
evidenceRequirement: A document showing the population estimate, its source and the reach calculation.
evidenceExamples: Market or segment sizing note | Reach calculation in annual report | Target setting paper

text: We have a written strategic plan with measurable targets that leaders review at least once a year.
anchor0: No written plan
anchor1: The plan is a funding proposal or concept note only
anchor2: A written plan exists but has no measurable targets or is over three years old
anchor3: A plan under three years old has measurable targets and was reviewed in the last 12 months
anchor4: A board approved plan under three years old has measurable targets, a budget linked to them, a review in the last 12 months and an annual progress report
evidenceRequirement: Current strategic plan and the latest annual review.
evidenceExamples: Strategic plan | Annual review minutes | Board approval minute

text: Our programme delivery model is written down well enough that a trained new team or a new location could run it.
anchor0: The model exists only in the heads of founders or key staff
anchor1: Slide decks or proposals describe the model but give no operating steps
anchor2: Some processes are documented with major gaps in selection, delivery or follow up
anchor3: A written manual covers selection, delivery, mentoring, follow up and data collection
anchor4: A written manual covers selection, delivery, mentoring, follow up and data collection, and two teams or sites have used it with documented adjustments
evidenceRequirement: Operating manual or standard procedures, and evidence of use by someone other than its authors.
evidenceExamples: Programme operations manual | Templates and checklists | Notes from a second team or site using it
riskTag: Delivery model not documented for scale

text: Before adding cohorts, locations or programmes, we check that we have enough staff, mentors and funding to keep quality.
anchor0: Expansion is decided when funding is offered, without a capacity check
anchor1: Leaders discuss capacity informally
anchor2: Capacity is checked for finance only
anchor3: A written capacity check covers staff, mentors, funding and quality for each expansion decision
anchor4: A written capacity check covers staff, mentors, funding and quality for each expansion decision, quality indicators are tracked afterwards and growth is paused if they fall
evidenceRequirement: Expansion decision notes showing a capacity check, and quality data after the last expansion.
evidenceExamples: Expansion proposal with capacity check | Board paper on growth | Quality indicators before and after

text: We select enterprises using written criteria that at least two reviewers score independently.
anchor0: Selection is by one person or personal contact, with no written criteria
anchor1: Criteria are understood informally and one person decides
anchor2: Written criteria exist but are not shared with applicants or not scored consistently
anchor3: Published criteria are scored by two or more reviewers on a scoring sheet
anchor4: Published criteria are scored by two or more reviewers on a scoring sheet, score differences are discussed, decisions are minuted and criteria are reviewed after each round
evidenceRequirement: Selection criteria, completed scoring sheets from at least two reviewers, and selection minutes for the last round.
evidenceExamples: Published call or criteria | Reviewer scoring sheets | Selection panel minutes

text: We keep a record of every applicant at every stage, with the reason for each selection or rejection.
anchor0: No application records are kept beyond selected enterprises
anchor1: Applications sit in email or paper files and are not collated
anchor2: A list of applicants and outcomes exists without reasons
anchor3: A database lists all applicants, the stage reached and the reason for each decision
anchor4: A database lists all applicants, the stage reached and the reason for each decision, and the data is analysed, for example by comparing selected with rejected applicants
evidenceRequirement: Applicant database or register for the last round, including rejected applicants.
evidenceExamples: Applicant register with outcomes | Rejection reason codes | Analysis of selected versus rejected applicants

text: We can show that we reach entrepreneurs who would not otherwise be supported, not only those already funded or well connected.
anchor0: Most participants were already funded or supported elsewhere, or this is not recorded
anchor1: Participants come mainly from leaders' own networks
anchor2: Some outreach beyond networks, but no data on prior support
anchor3: Application form records prior support, and at least half of participants had received none
anchor4: Application form records prior support and at least half of participants had none, results are compared for those with and without prior support, and outreach is adjusted
evidenceRequirement: Application data on prior support and the outreach plan.
evidenceExamples: Application form with prior support question | Share of participants with no prior support | Outreach plan and channels used

text: Each selected enterprise receives a baseline diagnostic that leads to a written support plan within 30 days of starting.
anchor0: Under 20 percent of the last cohort, or no baseline diagnostic is used
anchor1: 20 to 49 percent
anchor2: 50 to 74 percent
anchor3: 75 to 94 percent
anchor4: 95 percent or more, with support plans on file
evidenceRequirement: Diagnostic forms and support plans for the last cohort with dates. The verifier counts those done within 30 days.
evidenceExamples: Completed baseline diagnostics | Signed support plans | Cohort start date list
riskTag: No baseline diagnostic or support plan

text: Most of our support time goes to the needs entrepreneurs rank highest, such as sales, finance access or hiring, not mainly to pitch preparation.
anchor0: Support is mostly pitch decks and general workshops; needs are never asked
anchor1: Needs are asked at entry but support follows a fixed curriculum
anchor2: Some modules adapt to stated needs, and time use is not tracked
anchor3: Session or time records show most hours go to the top three needs the entrepreneurs ranked
anchor4: Session or time records show most hours go to the top three needs the entrepreneurs ranked, needs are re-ranked mid programme and support is re-planned where they changed
evidenceRequirement: Needs ranking from entrepreneurs and a session or time log showing where support hours went.
evidenceExamples: Needs ranking form | Mentor and coach session log | Hours by topic summary
riskTag: Support not matched to entrepreneur needs

text: Entrepreneur feedback on mentors and sessions leads to documented changes in how we deliver.
anchor0: No feedback is collected
anchor1: Informal comments are heard but nothing is recorded
anchor2: Feedback forms are collected but not analysed
anchor3: Feedback is analysed each cohort and at least one documented change was made
anchor4: Feedback is analysed each cohort and at least one documented change was made, changes are reported back to entrepreneurs and ratings are tracked across cohorts
evidenceRequirement: Feedback forms or survey results and the change record that followed.
evidenceExamples: Feedback summary by cohort | Change log or minutes citing feedback | Message to entrepreneurs on changes

text: Each entrepreneur is matched to a mentor or coach using a written view of the entrepreneur's needs and the mentor's expertise.
anchor0: Mentors are assigned by availability or personal contact, with no assessment
anchor1: Staff match by judgement and give no written reasons
anchor2: Matches are recorded but based only on sector, not on need
anchor3: Match records show the need and the mentor's expertise, and the entrepreneur may ask for a change
anchor4: Match records show the need and the mentor's expertise, the entrepreneur may ask for a change, match quality is tracked and mismatches are corrected within 30 days
evidenceRequirement: Match records for the last cohort and mentor profiles.
evidenceExamples: Mentor match sheet | Mentor profile database | Record of mentor changes requested

text: Market access support, such as buyer introductions or market information, is a deliberate part of our offer with named activities.
anchor0: No market access support is offered
anchor1: Occasional introductions happen when staff happen to know a buyer
anchor2: Market access sessions are included with no buyer or channel partner involved
anchor3: Planned market access activities name buyers or channels and record who took part
anchor4: Planned market access activities name buyers or channels and record who took part, and sales or contracts that result are tracked for participating enterprises
evidenceRequirement: Programme plan showing market access activities, buyer participation records and any sales tracking.
evidenceExamples: Buyer meeting attendance list | Market linkage activity plan | Contracts or orders recorded after linkage
riskTag: Market access not part of the offer

text: We have written criteria and a process for graduating, pausing or exiting enterprises from our programmes.
anchor0: No graduation or exit rules; enterprises drift
anchor1: Practice is informal and decided case by case
anchor2: Criteria are written for graduation only
anchor3: Written criteria and process for graduation, pausing and exit are applied to every enterprise
anchor4: Written criteria and process for graduation, pausing and exit are applied to every enterprise, decisions are recorded and exited enterprises get a closing review and referral
evidenceRequirement: Graduation and exit policy plus decision records for the last cohort.
evidenceExamples: Graduation criteria | Exit decision records | Closing review forms

text: We were in contact with most alumni of our last three cohorts during the past twelve months.
anchor0: Under 20 percent contacted, or there is no alumni list
anchor1: 20 to 39 percent contacted
anchor2: 40 to 59 percent contacted
anchor3: 60 to 79 percent contacted
anchor4: 80 percent or more contacted, with contact dates recorded
evidenceRequirement: Alumni list with dated contact records. The verifier calculates the share contacted in the last 12 months.
evidenceExamples: Alumni database with last contact date | Call or message log | Alumni event attendance

text: After the programme ends, alumni have a defined follow-up offer, such as clinics, mentor access or investor sessions, with clear eligibility.
anchor0: No support is offered after the programme ends
anchor1: Alumni can call staff for informal help
anchor2: Follow-up events are held occasionally for all alumni
anchor3: A written follow-up offer states eligibility, schedule and the responsible staff member
anchor4: A written follow-up offer states eligibility, schedule and the responsible staff member, is adjusted by alumni stage, and its uptake and outcomes are recorded
evidenceRequirement: The written alumni offer and records of alumni who used it.
evidenceExamples: Alumni support offer | Attendance or uptake records | Alumni follow-up budget line

text: Alumni contribute back to our programmes, for example as mentors, speakers or referrers of new applicants.
anchor0: No alumni involvement
anchor1: Alumni are invited to events only
anchor2: A few alumni speak or mentor informally, with no record
anchor3: Alumni roles are recorded and at least three alumni contributed in the last 12 months
anchor4: Alumni roles are recorded and at least three alumni contributed in the last 12 months, each with a defined role and briefing, and participants rate their contribution
evidenceRequirement: Records of alumni contributions in the last 12 months.
evidenceExamples: Alumni speaker or mentor list | Referral source data on applications | Participant ratings of alumni sessions

subDimensionName: Budgeting and cost per enterprise served
text: We know our programme cost per enterprise supported and can show how it is calculated.
anchor0: Cost per enterprise has never been calculated
anchor1: A rough figure comes from total budget divided by participants, with no written method
anchor2: Cost is calculated for some programmes using direct costs only
anchor3: Cost per enterprise is calculated for each programme, including shared costs, from the accounts
anchor4: Cost per enterprise is calculated for each programme from the accounts, including shared costs, tracked over cohorts and compared with results to judge value for money
evidenceRequirement: The calculation sheet and the accounts it draws on.
evidenceExamples: Cost per enterprise worksheet | Programme cost report from the accounting system | Value for money analysis

subDimensionName: Budgeting and cost per enterprise served
text: Each year our board or senior leaders approve a budget that shows income and costs by programme.
anchor0: There is no annual budget
anchor1: Budgets exist only inside funder proposals
anchor2: An organisation wide budget exists but not by programme, or it is not formally approved
anchor3: An approved annual budget shows income and costs by programme
anchor4: An approved annual budget shows income and costs by programme, a mid year revision is approved and variances are explained
evidenceRequirement: Approved annual budget and the minute that approved it.
evidenceExamples: Annual budget by programme | Board or leadership approval minute | Mid year revision

subDimensionName: Budgeting and cost per enterprise served
text: We share costs such as rent, management and shared staff across programmes using a written method.
anchor0: Shared costs are charged to whichever grant has money
anchor1: The finance person allocates shared costs informally
anchor2: An allocation rule exists for some costs and is applied inconsistently
anchor3: A written method is applied to all shared costs and used consistently across programmes
anchor4: A written method is applied consistently to all shared costs across programmes, is approved by the board or funders and is reviewed by auditors
evidenceRequirement: Written cost allocation policy and a sample of allocations in the accounts.
evidenceExamples: Cost allocation policy | Allocation journal entries | Auditor comment on allocation

subDimensionName: Budgeting and cost per enterprise served
text: We compare actual spending with budget at least monthly and act on large differences.
anchor0: No comparison of spending with budget
anchor1: Compared only when a funder asks
anchor2: Compared quarterly by the finance person with no leadership discussion
anchor3: Compared monthly by leaders, with differences above a set limit explained
anchor4: Compared monthly by leaders, with differences above a set limit explained, corrective actions recorded and checked the following month
evidenceRequirement: Budget versus actual reports for the last six months and the minutes that discuss them.
evidenceExamples: Monthly budget versus actual report | Leadership meeting minutes | Corrective action list

text: Our accounts for the last completed financial year were audited by an independent auditor.
anchor0: No audit or independent review in the last two years
anchor1: The audit is older than two years, or accounts are prepared in house only
anchor2: An independent review or examination was done, not a full audit
anchor3: A full audit for the last completed year was signed by a qualified firm more than six months after year end
anchor4: A full audit for the last completed year was signed within six months, with the management letter answered
evidenceRequirement: Signed audit report and management letter for the last completed year.
evidenceExamples: Signed audit report | Auditor management letter and response | Engagement letter

text: Our accounting system records income and spending by donor fund and programme code.
anchor0: Records are kept on paper or in one undifferentiated cashbook
anchor1: A spreadsheet cashbook is used without project coding
anchor2: A spreadsheet or software uses project codes but not for every transaction
anchor3: Accounting software with fund and programme codes is used for every transaction
anchor4: Accounting software with fund and programme codes is used for every transaction, and donor specific reports are produced without manual rework
evidenceRequirement: A system extract or trial balance showing fund and programme codes, and a donor report produced from it.
evidenceExamples: Accounting software extract | Chart of accounts with project codes | Donor financial report

text: No single person can approve a payment, make it and record it.
anchor0: One person approves, pays and records
anchor1: A second person signs only large payments
anchor2: Dual approval is in policy but not consistently evidenced
anchor3: Dual approval is documented, and the person who records differs from the approver and payer for all payments
anchor4: Dual approval is documented for all payments, recorder, approver and payer differ, approval limits are set by role, and auditors or the board tested them with no exceptions in a sample
evidenceRequirement: Payment approval policy and a sample of 10 payments with approval evidence.
evidenceExamples: Financial controls policy | Sample of payment vouchers | Bank mandate

text: We reconcile every bank and mobile money account to the cashbook each month.
anchor0: Fewer than 3 of the last 12 months, or no reconciliations
anchor1: 3 to 6 of the last 12 months
anchor2: 7 to 9 of the last 12 months
anchor3: 10 to 11 of the last 12 months
anchor4: All 12 months, each signed by a reviewer
evidenceRequirement: Monthly bank and mobile money reconciliations for the last 12 months.
evidenceExamples: Signed bank reconciliation statements | Mobile money statements | Cashbook

text: We submit donor and financial reports by the due dates set in our agreements.
anchor0: Under 50 percent on time, or not tracked
anchor1: 50 to 74 percent on time
anchor2: 75 to 89 percent on time
anchor3: 90 to 99 percent on time
anchor4: All reports on time in the last 12 months, managed with a reporting calendar
evidenceRequirement: Reporting calendar and submission dates for all reports due in the last 12 months.
evidenceExamples: Donor reporting calendar | Email submission receipts | Grant agreements with due dates

text: Our leaders receive management accounts every month, within 15 days of month end.
anchor0: No management accounts are produced
anchor1: Accounts are produced only for funders or audit
anchor2: Accounts are produced quarterly or later than 30 days after month end
anchor3: Accounts are produced monthly within 30 days and reviewed by the director
anchor4: Accounts are produced within 15 days of month end, include cash position, budget variance and funder balances, and are reviewed by the director and minuted
evidenceRequirement: Management accounts for the last three months with dates issued.
evidenceExamples: Monthly management accounts | Issue emails | Leadership minutes

text: We track spending against each donor's budget and eligible cost rules, so ineligible costs are found before the funder finds them.
anchor0: No tracking; funder queries often reveal errors
anchor1: Tracking happens only when a report is written
anchor2: A spreadsheet tracks spending by donor budget with no eligibility check
anchor3: Monthly tracking by donor budget line includes a documented eligibility check before payment
anchor4: Monthly tracking by donor budget line includes a documented eligibility check before payment, and the last two donor audits or reviews questioned no costs
evidenceRequirement: Donor budget tracking sheets and the latest funder or auditor findings.
evidenceExamples: Donor budget tracker | Eligibility checklist | Donor audit report
riskTag: Donor funds not tracked against rules

text: Our unrestricted reserves can cover core running costs for at least three months.
anchor0: No reserves, or under 1 month of core costs
anchor1: 1 to under 2 months
anchor2: 2 to under 3 months
anchor3: 3 to under 6 months
anchor4: 6 months or more, with a written reserves policy
evidenceRequirement: Bank statements and the budget. The verifier divides unrestricted cash by monthly core costs.
evidenceExamples: Bank balances for unrestricted accounts | Core cost budget | Reserves policy

text: We update a cash flow forecast for at least the next six months every month.
anchor0: No cash flow forecast
anchor1: A forecast is made once a year for the budget
anchor2: A forecast exists but covers under 3 months or is updated only quarterly
anchor3: A forecast covers 6 months and is updated monthly
anchor4: A 6 month forecast is updated monthly, includes funder payment dates, and has triggered early action on a shortfall
evidenceRequirement: The latest forecast and its update history.
evidenceExamples: Cash flow forecast file | Version history | Minutes where it was discussed

text: No single funder provided more than half of our income in the last financial year.
anchor0: One funder gave over 80 percent, or income shares are not known
anchor1: Largest funder gave 61 to 80 percent
anchor2: Largest funder gave 51 to 60 percent
anchor3: Largest funder gave 36 to 50 percent
anchor4: Largest funder gave 35 percent or less
evidenceRequirement: Audited or management accounts of income by source for the last financial year.
evidenceExamples: Income by funder schedule | Audited accounts note on income | Funder agreements

text: Part of our income is multi-year or core funding that is not tied to a single project.
anchor0: No such funding, or the share is not known
anchor1: Under 10 percent of last year's income
anchor2: 10 to 24 percent
anchor3: 25 to 49 percent
anchor4: 50 percent or more
evidenceRequirement: Funder agreements and income schedule showing multi-year or unrestricted income.
evidenceExamples: Multi-year grant agreement | Unrestricted income schedule | Core funding letter

text: We earn income from fees, services or success fees.
anchor0: No earned income, or the share is not known
anchor1: Under 5 percent of last year's income
anchor2: 5 to 14 percent
anchor3: 15 to 29 percent
anchor4: 30 percent or more, with prices set from cost data
evidenceRequirement: Income schedule showing earned income and the price setting method.
evidenceExamples: Fee schedule or price list | Earned income line in accounts | Invoices to enterprises or partners

text: We do not depend mainly on unrelated consulting work to keep the organisation running.
anchor0: Over 60 percent of income comes from work unrelated to our mission
anchor1: 41 to 60 percent
anchor2: 26 to 40 percent
anchor3: 11 to 25 percent
anchor4: 10 percent or less of income comes from unrelated work
evidenceRequirement: Income schedule split between mission work and unrelated work, checked against contracts.
evidenceExamples: Income by activity schedule | Consulting contracts | Programme budgets

subDimensionName: Investor and capital linkages for client enterprises
text: We record each introduction we make to investors, lenders or buyers and what came of it.
anchor0: Introductions are not recorded
anchor1: Staff remember introductions but there is no list
anchor2: A list of introductions exists without outcomes
anchor3: A register shows date, parties and outcome, updated at least every six months
anchor4: A register shows date, parties and outcome, is updated at least every six months, and records the value of deals confirmed by the enterprise or financier
evidenceRequirement: The introduction register and, for a sample of five, confirmation from the enterprise or financier.
evidenceExamples: Introduction register | Confirmation emails from financiers | Deal value summary

subDimensionName: Investor and capital linkages for client enterprises
text: Our investor and finance partners are active and suited to the stage and size of our enterprises.
anchor0: We have no investor or finance partners
anchor1: Partners appear mainly at pitch events
anchor2: Partners exist but several do not fit enterprise size or stage
anchor3: A partner list shows stage and ticket size fit, and at least half engaged in the last 12 months
anchor4: A partner list shows stage and ticket size fit, at least half of partners engaged in the last 12 months and at least one made an offer to our enterprises in that period
evidenceRequirement: Partner list with stage, ticket size and last engagement date.
evidenceExamples: Investor and lender partner list | Engagement log | Offers or term sheets received by enterprises

subDimensionName: Investor and capital linkages for client enterprises
text: We check an enterprise's records, numbers and documents with a coach before we introduce it to an investor or lender.
anchor0: Introductions are made with no preparation
anchor1: Enterprises receive pitch coaching only
anchor2: Some documents are checked with no standard list
anchor3: A standard readiness checklist is completed with a coach before each introduction
anchor4: A standard readiness checklist is completed with a coach before each introduction, its results feed into the support plan and investor feedback is collected
evidenceRequirement: Completed readiness checklists linked to introductions in the register.
evidenceExamples: Investor readiness checklist | Coach notes | Investor feedback forms

subDimensionName: Investor and capital linkages for client enterprises
text: We check that the finance offered through our partners has clear, fair terms before we encourage enterprises to take it.
anchor0: No review of terms; we promote any offer
anchor1: Terms are checked informally when enterprises ask
anchor2: Terms are reviewed for some partners with no written criteria
anchor3: Written criteria on cost, repayment and collateral are applied to each partner before promotion
anchor4: Written criteria on cost, repayment and collateral are applied to each partner before promotion, and enterprise complaints about partner terms are tracked and acted on
evidenceRequirement: Finance partner screening criteria and completed screens.
evidenceExamples: Partner screening checklist | Sample term sheets reviewed | Complaint log

text: Our working partnerships with other support organisations, government bodies, banks or buyers are written down, with each partner's role.
anchor0: No partnerships beyond informal contacts
anchor1: Partnerships are mentioned in proposals only
anchor2: Written MoUs exist for some partners but roles are unclear
anchor3: Written agreements for main partners state roles, referral rules and a contact person
anchor4: Written agreements for main partners state roles, referral rules and a contact person, are reviewed yearly, and at least one joint activity or referral per partner is recorded
evidenceRequirement: Partnership agreements and a record of joint work in the last 12 months.
evidenceExamples: MoUs | Referral records | Joint event reports

text: We keep a list of expected funding opportunities for the next 12 months, with the chance of winning and a person responsible for each.
anchor0: No funding pipeline
anchor1: Opportunities are tracked informally in emails
anchor2: A list exists without owners or chances
anchor3: A pipeline shows owner, amount, deadline and chance, reviewed monthly
anchor4: A pipeline shows owner, amount, deadline and chance, is reviewed monthly and compared with the budget gap, and the win rate is tracked
evidenceRequirement: The pipeline file and its latest review.
evidenceExamples: Funding pipeline tracker | Leadership meeting notes | Win rate calculation

text: We meet each major funder at least once a year to discuss results and future plans, beyond reporting requirements.
anchor0: We contact funders only when reports are due
anchor1: We contact funders only about problems
anchor2: We meet some major funders
anchor3: A yearly review meeting is held with every major funder and recorded
anchor4: A yearly review meeting is held with every major funder and recorded, and funder feedback led to a change in plan or agreement terms
evidenceRequirement: Meeting records with major funders in the last 12 months.
evidenceExamples: Funder meeting notes | Calendar invitations | Agreement amendments

text: When we agree funding, we ask for the real cost of delivery, including a fair share of running costs such as rent and management.
anchor0: We accept any budget offered, including none for running costs
anchor1: We accept low running cost shares because we fear losing funding
anchor2: We ask for a share on some grants without a rate based on our costs
anchor3: We apply a written rate based on our costs and report grants that fall short
anchor4: We apply a written rate based on our costs and report grants that fall short, and agreed rates cover our actual shared costs in most grants
evidenceRequirement: Written running cost policy and the rates agreed in the last three grants.
evidenceExamples: Running cost recovery policy | Grant budgets | Board paper on shortfalls
riskTag: Running costs not covered by funders

text: Our board or governing body meets regularly, with minutes and a quorum.
anchor0: No board, or no meeting in the last 12 months
anchor1: One meeting in the last 12 months
anchor2: Two or three meetings in the last 12 months
anchor3: Four or more meetings with minutes and a quorum
anchor4: Four or more meetings, minutes approved at the next meeting, over 75 percent attendance and actions tracked
evidenceRequirement: Board minutes and attendance records for the last 12 months.
evidenceExamples: Signed board minutes | Attendance register | Action tracker

text: Board members and senior staff sign a conflict of interest declaration each year, kept in a register.
anchor0: No conflict of interest rule
anchor1: A rule exists in the constitution but no declarations are signed
anchor2: Declarations were signed once and not renewed
anchor3: Annual signed declarations cover all board members and senior staff, with a register
anchor4: Annual signed declarations with a register cover all board members and senior staff, and minutes show declared conflicts and the member leaving the decision
evidenceRequirement: Conflict of interest policy, signed declarations and register for the current year.
evidenceExamples: Signed declarations | Conflicts register | Minutes noting a declared conflict

text: The board reviews the director's performance against agreed targets at least once a year.
anchor0: No review
anchor1: Informal feedback only
anchor2: A review is done but without written targets
anchor3: An annual written review against agreed targets is minuted
anchor4: An annual written review against agreed targets is minuted, with development actions and next year targets agreed and followed up
evidenceRequirement: Latest director review and the targets it used.
evidenceExamples: Director appraisal form | Board minute | Agreed targets

text: We have a written plan for who would lead the organisation if the director left unexpectedly.
anchor0: No plan; the organisation would stall
anchor1: Leaders assume someone will step in but nothing is written
anchor2: An acting arrangement is named for the director only
anchor3: A written plan names an acting lead and handover steps for the director and two key roles
anchor4: A written plan names an acting lead and handover steps for the director and two key roles, deputies are trained, and the plan was tested or updated in the last 12 months
evidenceRequirement: The succession or continuity plan and its last update.
evidenceExamples: Succession plan | Delegation of authority | Board minute approving it

text: Our core programme staff stay long enough for the organisation to keep what it has learned.
anchor0: Over 40 percent of core staff left in the last 12 months
anchor1: 26 to 40 percent left
anchor2: 16 to 25 percent left
anchor3: 6 to 15 percent left
anchor4: 5 percent or less left
evidenceRequirement: Staff list with start and end dates for the last 24 months. The verifier calculates leavers as a share of core staff.
evidenceExamples: Staff register | Exit records | Handover notes of leavers

text: When our own expertise is not enough, we bring in outside consultants or partners rather than promise services we cannot deliver.
anchor0: We promise services beyond our skills and deliver them poorly
anchor1: Outside help is used only after problems occur
anchor2: Outside experts are used sometimes with no rule for when
anchor3: Skills gaps are listed and outside experts are engaged under written terms
anchor4: Skills gaps are listed and outside experts are engaged under written terms, expert quality is reviewed and lessons are passed to staff
evidenceRequirement: Skills gap list and contracts or agreements with outside experts.
evidenceExamples: Skills gap analysis | Consultant contracts | Quality review of an expert's work

text: Every staff member received a documented performance review in the last 12 months.
anchor0: No reviews, or under 25 percent of staff reviewed
anchor1: 25 to 49 percent reviewed
anchor2: 50 to 74 percent reviewed
anchor3: 75 to 99 percent reviewed
anchor4: All staff reviewed, with a development plan for each
evidenceRequirement: Performance review records for all current staff.
evidenceExamples: Signed review forms | Development plans | Staff list

text: We vet mentors and coaches against written criteria, including references, before they work with entrepreneurs.
anchor0: No vetting; anyone willing can mentor
anchor1: Vetting is by personal recommendation only
anchor2: Written criteria exist but references and experience are not checked
anchor3: Written criteria are applied, and references and relevant experience are checked and filed for each mentor
anchor4: Written criteria are applied, references and relevant experience are checked and filed for each mentor, and mentors have a trial session or probation and periodic re-vetting
evidenceRequirement: Mentor selection criteria and the files of five active mentors.
evidenceExamples: Mentor selection criteria | Mentor files with references | Probation records

text: Each mentor signs a written agreement on hours, confidentiality, conduct and conflicts of interest before starting.
anchor0: No agreement or briefing
anchor1: Mentors get a verbal briefing only
anchor2: An agreement exists but few mentors signed it or it lacks conduct or conflict terms
anchor3: All active mentors signed an agreement covering hours, confidentiality, conduct and conflicts
anchor4: All active mentors signed an agreement covering hours, confidentiality, conduct and conflicts, renew it yearly and are briefed on the programme and safeguarding rules
evidenceRequirement: Signed agreements for all active mentors and the template.
evidenceExamples: Mentor agreement template | Signed agreements | Briefing attendance record

text: We review each mentor's activity and ratings from session logs at least once a year and decide whether to renew, coach or release them.
anchor0: No mentor records
anchor1: Staff recall who is active
anchor2: Session logs are kept but no individual mentor is reviewed
anchor3: A yearly review uses logs and ratings, and decisions are recorded
anchor4: A yearly review uses logs and ratings and records decisions, with weak mentors coached or released and strong mentors recognised
evidenceRequirement: Mentor session logs and the latest mentor review record.
evidenceExamples: Mentor session log | Annual mentor review | Release or renewal decision record

text: We have a written safeguarding policy, approved by our board, that covers staff, mentors, volunteers and the entrepreneurs we serve.
anchor0: No safeguarding policy
anchor1: A policy copied from another organisation, not adapted or approved
anchor2: An approved policy that does not cover mentors or sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment
anchor3: A board approved policy covers staff, mentors and participants, including sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment
anchor4: A board approved policy covers staff, mentors and participants, including sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment, adds child safeguarding for under 18s, and was reviewed within 24 months
evidenceRequirement: The safeguarding policy, its approval minute and review date.
evidenceExamples: Safeguarding policy | Board approval minute | Code of conduct

text: We run a complaints channel that entrepreneurs know about and that accepts confidential reports.
anchor0: No complaints channel
anchor1: Entrepreneurs may speak to staff but there is no defined channel
anchor2: A channel exists, such as a phone number or box, but entrepreneurs were not told or no confidential option exists
anchor3: A confidential channel is explained at onboarding, and cases are logged and handled by a named person
anchor4: A confidential channel is explained at onboarding and cases are logged and handled by a named person, with timely resolution, protection from retaliation and a yearly summary to the board
evidenceRequirement: Description of the channel, onboarding material that explains it, and the case log.
evidenceExamples: Complaints procedure | Onboarding pack | Case log

text: Staff and mentors complete safeguarding and code of conduct training before they work with entrepreneurs.
anchor0: No training, or under 25 percent trained
anchor1: 25 to 59 percent of active staff and mentors trained
anchor2: 60 to 84 percent trained
anchor3: 85 to 99 percent trained, with attendance records
anchor4: All trained before starting, and refreshed in the last 12 months
evidenceRequirement: Training attendance records for all active staff and mentors.
evidenceExamples: Training attendance register | Training materials | Induction checklist
riskTag: Staff and mentors not trained on safeguarding

text: We keep all client enterprise records in one database, with a unique ID for each enterprise.
anchor0: Records are scattered across personal files, phones and paper
anchor1: Several spreadsheets hold duplicate or conflicting entries
anchor2: One central spreadsheet or tool exists but has no unique ID, or duplicates are found
anchor3: A central database has unique IDs and shows no duplicates in a sample of 20 records
anchor4: A central database has unique IDs, shows no duplicates in a sample of 20 records, and has data entry rules and a change history
evidenceRequirement: A live demonstration of the database and a check of 20 records for duplicates.
evidenceExamples: Client database | Unique ID field | Sample of 20 records

text: Applicant, participant and alumni records are linked in one system, so we can follow each enterprise from application to alumni.
anchor0: Applicants, participants and alumni are kept apart or not kept
anchor1: Participants are recorded but applicants and alumni are not
anchor2: Applicants and participants are linked but alumni are not followed
anchor3: All three stages are linked by unique ID, and a sample enterprise can be traced end to end in ten minutes
anchor4: All three stages are linked by unique ID, a sample enterprise can be traced end to end in ten minutes, and status is updated at least yearly and used for outcome analysis
evidenceRequirement: A live trace of three enterprises from application to alumni status.
evidenceExamples: Database showing all three stages | Trace of a sample enterprise | Yearly status update

text: Our client database has complete data on the fields we report on, such as gender, age, location, revenue and jobs.
anchor0: Under 40 percent complete, or completeness is not checked
anchor1: 40 to 59 percent complete
anchor2: 60 to 79 percent complete
anchor3: 80 to 94 percent complete
anchor4: 95 percent or more complete, with missing data followed up
evidenceRequirement: A database extract for the last cohort. The verifier calculates the share of key fields filled in.
evidenceExamples: Client database extract | Completeness check | Follow up log for missing data

text: We have a written guide that defines each data field and indicator and how it is collected.
anchor0: No definitions; each person records differently
anchor1: Definitions are known verbally by one person
anchor2: Definitions exist for some indicators
anchor3: A written data guide defines all reported fields and collection methods, and staff are trained
anchor4: A written data guide defines all reported fields and collection methods, staff are trained, a second person checks quality and the guide is updated yearly
evidenceRequirement: The data guide or dictionary and training records.
evidenceExamples: Data dictionary | Indicator reference sheets | Training attendance

text: We have defined indicators with baseline values for our entrepreneurs, such as revenue, jobs and finance accessed.
anchor0: No indicators or baselines
anchor1: Indicators are listed in proposals but no baselines are collected
anchor2: Baselines are collected for some indicators or some cohorts
anchor3: Indicators and baselines are recorded for every participant in the last cohort
anchor4: Indicators and baselines are recorded for every participant in the last cohort, tied to the theory of change and reviewed yearly
evidenceRequirement: Indicator list and baseline data for the last cohort.
evidenceExamples: Indicator framework | Baseline data for the last cohort | Annual indicator review

text: We follow up enterprises after the programme ends and collect outcome data, not only during the programme.
anchor0: No follow up after the programme
anchor1: Under 25 percent of alumni followed up at 12 months
anchor2: 25 to 49 percent followed up at 12 months
anchor3: 50 to 74 percent followed up at 12 months
anchor4: 75 percent or more followed up at 12 months or later
evidenceRequirement: Follow up survey or call records for the cohort that ended about 12 months ago.
evidenceExamples: Follow up survey responses | Outcome data for alumni | Response rate calculation
riskTag: No outcome tracking after the programme

text: When we report results, we use a comparison group or state how much of the change we can and cannot attribute to our programme.
anchor0: All change in participants is claimed as programme impact
anchor1: Results are reported as before and after with no discussion of other causes
anchor2: Limits are mentioned in reports but not estimated
anchor3: A written attribution method, such as a comparison group or other estimate, is used and its limits stated
anchor4: Participants were compared with waitlisted or rejected applicants for at least one cohort and findings reported
evidenceRequirement: Evaluation or results report showing the attribution method.
evidenceExamples: Results report with method section | Comparison group data | Attribution note

text: We check a sample of reported results against documents such as sales records, bank statements or payroll, not only entrepreneur statements.
anchor0: All results are self reported and unchecked
anchor1: Staff use judgement but keep no checks
anchor2: Large claims are occasionally checked, unrecorded
anchor3: At least 10 percent of reported results are checked against documents each reporting period and recorded
anchor4: At least 10 percent of reported results are checked against documents each period and recorded, errors are corrected and error rates reported, and a third party reviewed this within 24 months
evidenceRequirement: Verification records for the last reporting period.
evidenceExamples: Verification checklist | Copies of supporting documents | Error rate summary

text: Our leaders use results data to decide which programmes to continue, change or stop.
anchor0: Decisions never refer to results data
anchor1: Results are mentioned in discussion with no records
anchor2: Results are presented to leaders but decisions are not linked to them
anchor3: Decision records cite results data for at least one continue, change or stop decision in the last 12 months
anchor4: Decision records cite results data for at least one continue, change or stop decision in the last 12 months, using rules agreed in advance, and a programme was redesigned or stopped as a result
evidenceRequirement: Leadership or board minutes that cite results in decisions.
evidenceExamples: Board or leadership minutes | Programme review papers | Decision record

text: We report disappointing or negative results to our board and funders, not only successes.
anchor0: Reports show only successes
anchor1: Weak results are mentioned only if a funder asks
anchor2: Weak results are shown to the board but not to funders
anchor3: Annual reports to board and funders include indicators that missed target, with reasons
anchor4: Annual reports to board and funders include indicators that missed target with reasons, list lessons and corrective actions, and are shared publicly at least yearly
evidenceRequirement: Latest board and funder reports.
evidenceExamples: Annual results report | Funder report | Public learning note

text: After each cohort we hold a structured review with staff and entrepreneurs and record the changes we will make.
anchor0: No review
anchor1: An informal staff chat with nothing recorded
anchor2: A staff only review is recorded
anchor3: A review with staff and entrepreneur input follows each cohort, with written actions
anchor4: A review with staff and entrepreneur input follows each cohort with written actions, and the next review checks that earlier actions were completed
evidenceRequirement: Review reports for the last two cohorts.
evidenceExamples: After cohort review report | Action list | Entrepreneur input notes

text: Each major programme is reviewed against relevance, effectiveness, efficiency and sustainability at least once per funding cycle.
anchor0: No review or evaluation of any programme
anchor1: Only a funder required final report, with no assessment of effectiveness
anchor2: An internal review covers outputs only
anchor3: A written review covers the four criteria for each major programme in the last funding cycle
anchor4: A written review covers the four criteria for each major programme in the last funding cycle, is carried out or checked by an external evaluator, and has a recorded management response
evidenceRequirement: Programme review or evaluation reports from the last funding cycle.
evidenceExamples: Evaluation report | Programme review using the four criteria | Management response

text: Our organisation's legal registration and annual filings with the Registrar of Companies are up to date.
anchor0: Not registered, or annual returns missing for two or more years
anchor2: Registered, but annual returns are late or missing for one year
anchor4: Registered with a current certificate and all annual returns filed
evidenceRequirement: Certificate of incorporation and proof of filing of annual returns, including beneficial ownership information, for the years due.
evidenceExamples: Certificate of incorporation | Annual return filing receipts | Beneficial ownership filing
riskTag: Registration or annual returns not current

text: We hold a current licence as a non-profit organisation from the NPO Secretariat and renew it on time.
anchor0: No licence, or the licence expired more than three months ago
anchor2: A provisional licence, or a licence expired within the last three months
anchor4: A final licence is current and renewals are on schedule
evidenceRequirement: NPO licence and renewal filings.
evidenceExamples: NPO licence | Renewal application and receipt | Tax clearance certificate used for renewal

text: Our tax registration and returns with the Ghana Revenue Authority are up to date.
anchor0: Not registered for tax, or tax arrears are in dispute
anchor1: Registered, with returns filed irregularly and arrears outstanding
anchor2: Registered, with one or more returns late or missing in the last 12 months
anchor3: All returns filed in the last 12 months with no arrears
anchor4: All returns filed in the last 12 months with no arrears, a valid tax clearance certificate held and a filing calendar in use
evidenceRequirement: Tax registration and filing receipts for the last 12 months.
evidenceExamples: Tax identification registration | Filing receipts | Tax clearance certificate

text: We remit statutory staff deductions, such as SSNIT contributions and PAYE, on time.
anchor0: Staff are employed without registration or deductions
anchor1: Deductions are made but remitted irregularly
anchor2: Deductions are remitted most months, with some late payments in the last 12 months
anchor3: All deductions were remitted on time in the last 12 months, with receipts
anchor4: All deductions were remitted on time in the last 12 months, with receipts, and payroll records are reconciled to remittances each quarter
evidenceRequirement: Payroll records and remittance receipts for the last 12 months.
evidenceExamples: Payroll register | SSNIT and tax remittance receipts | Quarterly reconciliation

text: Our organisation is registered with the Data Protection Commission and the registration is current.
anchor0: Not registered while we hold personal data of entrepreneurs
anchor2: Registered, but the registration lapsed or its details are out of date
anchor4: Registration is current and the renewal date is tracked
evidenceRequirement: Data Protection Commission registration certificate and renewal date.
evidenceExamples: Registration certificate | Renewal receipt | Compliance report submitted at renewal
riskTag: Not registered with the Data Protection Commission

text: We obtain informed consent from entrepreneurs, explained in plain language, on what personal data we collect, why, and who will see it.
anchor0: No notice and no consent record
anchor1: A verbal explanation only
anchor2: A notice exists but consent is not recorded for all, or sharing with funders or investors is not mentioned
anchor3: A written privacy notice and signed consent cover all participants and sharing with funders and investors
anchor4: A written privacy notice and signed consent cover all participants and sharing with funders and investors, with separate consent for photos and testimonies and a way to withdraw consent
evidenceRequirement: Privacy notice and signed consent forms for a sample of 10 participants.
evidenceExamples: Privacy notice | Signed consent forms | Photo and testimony consent forms

text: We protect personal data with technical and organisational security measures and have a procedure for data breaches.
anchor0: No safeguards; data sits on personal phones or shared passwords
anchor1: Passwords are used but there are no backups or rules
anchor2: Basic safeguards such as passwords and backup exist but no written rules or breach procedure
anchor3: Written security rules, role based access, regular backups and a breach procedure are in place
anchor4: Written security rules, role based access, regular backups and a breach procedure are in place, staff are trained and the measures were tested or reviewed in the last 12 months
evidenceRequirement: Data security policy, a demonstration of access controls and the breach procedure.
evidenceExamples: Data security policy | Access control settings | Breach response procedure

text: We keep a risk register with owners and review it at least every quarter.
anchor0: No risk register
anchor1: Risks are discussed informally with no list
anchor2: A risk list exists, has no owners and has not been reviewed in six months
anchor3: A register with owners and actions is reviewed at least twice a year
anchor4: A register of programme, financial, safeguarding and reputation risks has owners and actions, is reviewed at least twice a year and is reviewed quarterly by the board
evidenceRequirement: Current risk register and review minutes.
evidenceExamples: Risk register | Review minutes | Board paper on risks

text: We check funders, partners and major donors before accepting money or agreements, for example their source of funds and reputation.
anchor0: We accept any funding or partnership offered
anchor1: Informal enquiries are made
anchor2: Checks are made for some new funders
anchor3: A written due diligence checklist is applied to every new funder and partner
anchor4: A written due diligence checklist is applied to every new funder and partner, with periodic re-checks and recorded decisions to decline funding
evidenceRequirement: Due diligence checklist and completed checks for the last three new funders or partners.
evidenceExamples: Due diligence checklist | Completed checks | Decline decision record

text: We verify basic facts about an enterprise, such as registration, ownership and key claims, before we endorse it or introduce it to an investor.
anchor0: No verification
anchor1: We rely on what the entrepreneur tells us
anchor2: Registration only is checked
anchor3: A checklist verifies registration, ownership and main claims with documents before every introduction
anchor4: A checklist verifies registration, ownership and main claims with documents before every introduction, checks are recorded and investor feedback on accuracy is tracked
evidenceRequirement: Verification checklists linked to introductions in the register.
evidenceExamples: Verification checklist | Copies of registration documents | Investor feedback on accuracy
riskTag: Enterprise claims not verified before endorsement

text: We have a written anti-fraud and anti-corruption policy that staff, mentors and board members have read and signed.
anchor0: No policy
anchor1: A general statement appears in the code of conduct only
anchor2: A policy exists but is unsigned or not shared
anchor3: The policy is signed by all staff and board members and sets out reporting steps
anchor4: The policy sets out reporting steps and is signed by all staff, board members, mentors and partners, with an annual refresher and a case log
evidenceRequirement: The anti-fraud policy and signed acknowledgements.
evidenceExamples: Anti-fraud policy | Signed acknowledgements | Training record

text: We buy goods and services using written procurement rules that require quotations above a set amount.
anchor0: No rules; staff choose suppliers
anchor1: An informal rule only
anchor2: Written rules exist but are applied inconsistently
anchor3: Written rules set thresholds and minimum quotations, and purchase records show them applied in the last 12 months
anchor4: Written rules set thresholds and minimum quotations, purchase records show them applied in the last 12 months, an independent person approves and auditors tested a sample
evidenceRequirement: Procurement policy and files for the last five purchases above the threshold.
evidenceExamples: Procurement policy | Quotation files | Purchase approval records

text: Suspected fraud or misuse of funds is recorded, investigated and reported to the board and affected funders.
anchor0: No procedure; incidents are hidden or handled privately
anchor1: Incidents are handled case by case and not recorded
anchor2: Incidents are reported to the board only
anchor3: A written procedure applies; incidents are logged, investigated and reported to the board and funders as required
anchor4: A written procedure applies, incidents are logged, investigated and reported to the board and funders as required, lessons change controls and the board gets an annual summary
evidenceRequirement: Incident procedure and the incident log, including nil returns.
evidenceExamples: Incident response procedure | Incident log | Board report on incidents

text: Women make up a meaningful share of the people who decide which enterprises we select.
anchor0: No women on selection decisions, or there is no panel
anchor1: Women are under 20 percent of the panel
anchor2: Women are 20 to 29 percent of the panel
anchor3: Women are 30 to 39 percent of the panel
anchor4: Women are 40 percent or more of the panel
evidenceRequirement: Panel lists for the last two selection rounds.
evidenceExamples: Selection panel list | Panel minutes | Panel terms of reference

text: Each year we review our selection, curriculum and mentoring for barriers facing women and young people, such as timing, venue, childcare or biased scoring.
anchor0: No review of barriers
anchor1: Informal discussion only
anchor2: A review was done once with no changes
anchor3: An annual written review finds barriers and at least one change was made
anchor4: An annual written review finds barriers with participant input, at least one change was made and its effect was checked in the next cohort
evidenceRequirement: Latest barrier review and the changes made.
evidenceExamples: Barrier review report | Programme change record | Participant input notes
riskTag: No review for gender or youth barriers

text: We set written targets for women and young people in each cohort and report against them.
anchor0: No targets
anchor1: A verbal aim only
anchor2: Targets are set for some programmes and not reported
anchor3: Written targets for every programme are reported to the board each year
anchor4: Written targets for every programme are reported to the board each year, and corrective action was recorded after the last cohort that missed a target
evidenceRequirement: Targets and the latest report against them.
evidenceExamples: Inclusion targets | Board report | Corrective action note

text: We compare outcomes such as revenue, jobs and finance raised for women and men and for different age groups each year.
anchor0: Outcomes are never split by gender or age
anchor1: Participation counts are split but outcomes are not
anchor2: Outcomes are split for one indicator in the last year
anchor3: Revenue, jobs and finance outcomes are split by gender and age each year in a written analysis
anchor4: Revenue, jobs and finance outcomes are split by gender and age each year in a written analysis, and a documented change in support was made to close a gap found
evidenceRequirement: The latest outcome analysis by gender and age.
evidenceExamples: Disaggregated results report | Support change record | Database extract
riskTag: Results not split by gender or age

text: We help entrepreneurs assess the climate and environmental risks and opportunities in their businesses.
anchor0: Not covered in our programmes
anchor1: Mentioned in a session only
anchor2: A climate or environment module is offered to some participants
anchor3: Every entrepreneur completes a climate and environmental risk check as part of the diagnostic or plan
anchor4: Every entrepreneur completes a climate and environmental risk check as part of the diagnostic or plan, actions are tracked and the share adopting at least one measure is reported
evidenceRequirement: Programme materials and completed risk checks for the last cohort.
evidenceExamples: Climate risk check form | Module slides | Completed checks
riskTag: Climate risk not addressed with enterprises

text: We screen enterprises we promote or link to finance for serious environmental or social harm, and decline or set conditions where we find it.
anchor0: No screening
anchor1: Informal judgement only
anchor2: A screening question is on the application but not acted on
anchor3: A written exclusion list and checklist are used before promotion or finance linkage
anchor4: A written exclusion list and checklist are used before promotion or finance linkage, decisions are logged and conditions are followed up
evidenceRequirement: Screening policy and completed screens linked to introductions.
evidenceExamples: Exclusion list | Completed screening checklist | Decision log

text: We can call on climate and environment expertise through staff, mentors or partners, such as universities or specialist agencies, when entrepreneurs need it.
anchor0: No access to such expertise
anchor1: Occasional personal contacts only
anchor2: Expert partners are named with no agreement
anchor3: At least one written agreement or expert roster was used in the last 12 months
anchor4: At least one written agreement or expert roster was used in the last 12 months, the expertise served several enterprises and feedback was recorded
evidenceRequirement: Expert roster or partnership agreements and records of use.
evidenceExamples: Expert roster | MoU with a university or agency | Session records

text: We track climate or environmental results, such as the number of enterprises adopting resource efficient or climate smart practices.
anchor0: No tracking
anchor1: Anecdotes only
anchor2: Tracked for a few enterprises in one cohort
anchor3: An indicator is defined and tracked across all cohorts in the last 12 months
anchor4: An indicator is defined and tracked across all cohorts in the last 12 months and reported to funders with baseline and follow up data
evidenceRequirement: Indicator definition and data for the last 12 months.
evidenceExamples: Climate indicator data | Follow up survey | Funder report section

subDimensionName: Ecosystem contribution and reach to rural and underserved enterprises
text: We reach rural entrepreneurs through design choices such as location, language and delivery method, not only through open calls.
anchor0: Open calls only, with all activity in the capital or a regional city
anchor1: Rural applicants are welcome but nothing in the design changed
anchor2: Some rural outreach, but sessions still require travel to the city
anchor3: Delivery in district or community locations, local languages and low data options is planned in the design
anchor4: Delivery in district or community locations, local languages and low data options is planned in the design, rural entrepreneurs helped design it and results are reviewed by location
evidenceRequirement: Programme design showing rural delivery choices and the locations used.
evidenceExamples: Delivery plan with locations | Materials in local languages | Low data delivery options

subDimensionName: Ecosystem contribution and reach to rural and underserved enterprises
text: We know what share of our participants are based outside the regional capital and compare it with a written target or the spread of enterprises in our area.
anchor0: Participant location is not recorded
anchor1: Location is recorded but the share is not calculated
anchor2: The share is calculated with no target or comparison
anchor3: The share is compared with a written target or local enterprise spread and reviewed yearly
anchor4: The share is compared with a written target or local enterprise spread and reviewed yearly, and action was taken in the last 12 months where it fell below target
evidenceRequirement: Client database location data and the target or comparison document.
evidenceExamples: Participants by location report | Rural reach target | Review minutes

subDimensionName: Ecosystem contribution and reach to rural and underserved enterprises
text: We reduce cost and access barriers for participants, such as transport, data costs, fee waivers or accessible venues.
anchor0: Participants bear all costs and venues are not accessible
anchor1: Occasional help is given on request
anchor2: Support covers some costs in some programmes
anchor3: A written support budget covers transport or data costs and venues are accessible to people with disabilities
anchor4: A written support budget covers transport or data costs and venues are accessible to people with disabilities, use is tracked and drop outs for cost reasons are reviewed
evidenceRequirement: Support budget lines, venue checks and drop out records.
evidenceExamples: Participant support budget | Venue accessibility checklist | Drop out reasons log

subDimensionName: Ecosystem contribution and reach to rural and underserved enterprises
text: We share our curriculum, tools or findings with other support organisations or policy makers.
anchor0: Nothing is shared
anchor1: We share informally on request only
anchor2: Something was shared once in the last 12 months
anchor3: At least two sharing activities in the last 12 months, such as open materials, ecosystem meetings or policy briefs
anchor4: At least two sharing activities in the last 12 months, such as open materials, ecosystem meetings or policy briefs, with evidence that others adopted our tools or findings
evidenceRequirement: Records of sharing activities in the last 12 months.
evidenceExamples: Published materials | Ecosystem meeting records | Policy brief or letter
riskTag: Learning not shared with the ecosystem
